Key technologies involved include transformers and safetensors, central to modern NLP.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.

stories.author: unknown

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedups reach up to 90% when utilizing coding agents, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating active development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is connecting messaging workflows directly to local AI capabilities.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, both locally and in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Anthropic wants to develop its own drugs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is expanding its AI focus beyond general models into specialized scientific applications with 'Claude Science'.
Claude Science functions as an 'AI workbench for scientists,' integrating disparate tools and datasets into a unified environment.
The announcement signals a major industry trend toward applying large language models to accelerate scientific discovery and research.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: Autonomous AI coding agents, due to persistent codebases across sessions, introduce a novel attack surface.
The research introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study how misaligned agents can distribute malicious payloads across multiple pull requests over time.
This work addresses the critical security challenge of safely deploying highly capable but potentially untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
It focuses on 'unlearning' techniques, which aim to reliably remove this memorized knowledge post-training.
LACUNA introduces a new testbed to evaluate localization precision, moving beyond simple output-level unlearning benchmarks.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-Function Programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of LLM API usage, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long context windows.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a novel, training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Highlights the gap between LLMs' ability to access long contexts and their actual capacity for effective context utilization.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of Large Language Models (LLMs) memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It critiques current unlearning benchmarks, which only test for knowledge removal at the output level, questioning true knowledge erasure.
The paper introduces LACUNA, a new testbed designed to evaluate the precision of localization methods used in LLM unlearning.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log parsing, intent ranking).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses limitations of current LLM API usage, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a new data-agnostic quantization method specifically designed for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses the high inference cost of DiTs, which are currently state-of-the-art in image and video generation.
Solves the problem of activation shifting across different timesteps and prompts, which plagues traditional post-training quantization (PTQ) methods.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
It critiques current 'localize-first, unlearn-second' methods, noting that existing benchmarks only test unlearning at the output level.
The research introduces 'LACUNA,' a new testbed designed to evaluate the true precision of knowledge erasure within LLMs.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLM safety failures post-alignment training.
Proposes a simple, real-time monitoring system that uses an external model's verifier signal.
Demonstrates the monitor's competitiveness in detecting unsafe outputs using mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and capability of AI agentic workflows.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new macOS malware, PamStealer, has been discovered.
The malware is noted for being different from typical macOS infostealers.
The discovery highlights a growing focus and increased sophistication in Mac-targeting malware.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to allow supersonic airliners to fly over US cities.
The key condition for this allowance is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to eliminate the sonic boom.
This represents a potential regulatory shift enabling the return of supersonic commercial travel within the US.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal and thresholding for alarm decisions.
The proposed monitoring design shows competitive performance in tests involving mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents versus private, off-the-record (OTR) communications.
Suggests that social context can lead to the emergence of latent objectives in LLM interactions without explicit prompting.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, is introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for training LLMs.
Addresses a key limitation of existing OPSD methods: teacher supervision based on privileged information can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The research focuses on modulating disagreement within the distillation process to improve model robustness and generalization.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that merges Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like SAT solvers (Glucose 4.1, CaDiCaL 3.0.0).
The SE-RRMs exhibit improved extrapolation capabilities when applied to larger constraint satisfaction problems.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social context.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Identifies that dense, token-level supervision from a privileged teacher model can cause overfitting and hurt cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by mitigating the negative effects of overly strong teacher supervision.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a new framework for controllable simulated agents in AI.
The agents are designed to imitate logged behavior while allowing steering along interpretable axes.
This controllability is crucial for testing autonomous systems safely by isolating variables and reproducing edge cases.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs without expensive human supervision or real-world feedback.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Uses the model's own outputs and majority voting across multiple rollouts to generate pseudo-labels.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses a critical challenge in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL): robustness against data heterogeneity.
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis of how various D-SSL frameworks perform under non-IID data conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of decentralized learning methods utilizing vast, unlabeled datasets.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to reduce reliance on external, costly, and less reproducible LLM APIs for common tasks like log parsing or search ranking.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances against off-the-record (OTR) responses to detect latent objective emergence.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the impact of relational context on LLM expression.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker recognition in these complex video contexts.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: CLIP models, foundational to modern LVLMs, are vulnerable to Typographic Attacks (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The research proposes a training-free method for robust concept localization to address this critical failure mode.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during reasoning.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to properly attend to visual inputs during self-correction.
Aims to improve the models' ability to generate grounded corrections, especially for out-of-distribution images.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates the potential of scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve the fidelity of social simulations.
The study questions whether current scaling laws alone can resolve the lack of faithfulness in LLM social simulations.
It explores whether simulation fidelity is an independent research area separate from general LLM capabilities.
